checks.finding: design.md '## Design Decisions' table (lines 22-30) states a rationale for every row DD-1..DD-7. DD-1: distinguished_from needs cross-context references, so a nested structure would double the resolution rule; JSON Schema draft-07 cannot express referential integrity so membership enforcement is pushed to the validator (INV-003, plan review P-7). DD-2: 'owner 決定（2026-08-16）: v1 資産は存在しない'. DD-3: a cross-file $ref would create fragile coupling with v1 deletion (OQ-001) and duplication drift is constrained by TEST-001/002. DD-4: explicit comparison against jq/ajv/Test-Json with reasons for exclusion (INV-005 house pattern, PS5.1/Test-Json incompatibility). DD-5: cites INV-006's existing convention. DD-6: resolves OQ-004's proposal and avoids duplicating v1's existing validation path. DD-7: gate needs machine-consumable per-line violations, fail-closed non-zero exit. No inline decision in design.md lacks an accompanying rationale clause.

design.md has no '## Open Questions' heading; the closest section is '## Open Items' (design.md:148-154). Repository-wide grep across all 38 spec design.md files shows sdd-domain-concept-contract/design.md is the only one that does not use the '## Open Questions' heading (37 use it directly; the design.template.md at plugins/sdd-bootstrap/skills/sdd-bootstrap-interviewer/templates/design.template.md:99-107 requires 'Owner:', 'Blocks Implementation: yes | no', and 'Resolution Path:' fields per entry). Neither entry in '## Open Items' carries these fields: OQ-001 ('v1 ファイルの最終処遇') defers to 'Phase 3' without naming a resolving role, has no literal 'Blocks Implementation:' field, and no literal 'Resolution Path:' field (only prose 'Phase 3 で判断'). OQ-003 is stated as already resolved ('確定') so it is not an outstanding open item. Concrete failure mode: a Phase-3 implementer or reviewer scanning design.md cannot mechanically determine who owns the v1-disposition decision or whether it gates Phase-0 sign-off. Per the check's explicit rule, 'An open question with no owner is a Major finding.'

design.md has no separate '## Assumptions' section (its headings are Technical Summary, Design Decisions, v2 Schema Shape, Architecture, Error Handling, Test Strategy, Constraint Compliance, Open Items — confirmed by heading scan). investigation.md is present (not absent), so the fallback trigger requiring investigation.md ('investigation.md absent; design has <N> non-trivial assumptions...') does not activate. The assumptions embedded in the Design Decisions table are each individually grounded: DD-1/DD-3 cite INV-003; DD-4/DD-5 cite INV-005/INV-006; DD-2 cites an explicit dated owner decision (2026-08-16); DD-6 resolves OQ-004 by explicit proposal. No ungrounded, non-trivial assumption is present in design.md.

design.md HAS a '## Constraint Compliance' section (lines 138-146, a 5-row table: v1 無変更/hook-guard 保護/content-as-data/外部依存禁止/ASCII改行規約), so the Primary/TYPE-D branch applies. requirements.md '## Security Boundaries' states a third, distinct security constraint not mirrored in that table: 'fixture に秘密情報・実在の個人情報を含めない' (fixtures must not contain secrets or real personal data). This constraint is not addressed anywhere in design.md — not as a Constraint Compliance row, and not in any other section (Technical Summary, Design Decisions, v2 Schema Shape, Architecture, Error Handling, Test Strategy, Open Items were all checked; none restates or complies with it). Concrete failure mode: security-spec.md's own Threat Considerations note that seed/interview material can carry 'external text (issue bodies, article excerpts)' into hand-written fixtures — exactly the vector this constraint guards against — yet design.md's Test Strategy section (which defines the 73-fixture negative corpus plus 5 positive fixture families) gives no design-level directive against it, and the Constraint Compliance ledger (this check's designated rollup) omits it entirely. Per the check's Primary/TYPE-D rule, 'A constraint with no compliance statement is a Critical finding.'

No performance requirements found in requirements.md. No numeric latency/throughput/concurrency/SLA threshold appears anywhere in the document. The only size-bound note (Edge Cases: '契約ファイルが10MBを超える等の異常入力: validator は fail-closed で非0終了') is a fail-closed input-size boundary for malformed/oversized-input handling, not a performance or response-time target.
